A production facility is required to synthesize an intertemporal procurement and inventory-control policy for a mission-critical raw material over a finite, discretely indexed planning horizon of 6 days.
At the inception of the horizon (prior to period 1), the system is endowed with an initial on-hand stock of 60 units.
In each period t = 1, ..., 6, the decision-maker may submit a replenishment order to an upstream supplier, subject to an admissible-order constraint stipulating that the order quantity must lie within the closed interval [18, 30] units.
Replenishment is subject to a deterministic, strictly positive lead time: any order placed in period t is realized only after 1 day(s), at which point the delivered material can be deployed to satisfy contemporaneous demand or to augment the inventory state.
The exogenously specified demand stream for the material over the planning horizon is given by the following deterministic profile:
* Period 1: demand 54 units
* Period 2: demand 35 units
* Period 3: demand 22 units
* Period 4: demand 26 units
* Period 5: demand 32 units
* Period 6: demand 56 units

Inventory shortfalls are allowed within the model; however, any demand that remains unfilled in the period of its occurrence is interpreted as lost sales and is not propagated forward as backlog to subsequent periods.
Material quantities are modeled as continuous decision variables, and the storage subsystem is governed by a hard capacity constraint: at no point in time may the on-hand inventory exceed 60 units.
The total cost accumulated over the planning horizon comprises three components: an ordering cost of 1 per unit ordered; a holding cost of 3 per unit of inventory carried from one period to the next; and a shortage (lost-demand) penalty of 8 per unit of unmet demand.
Your task is to specify, for each period t, the order quantity so as to induce an evolution of the inventory and shortage levels that minimizes the aggregate cost over the entire planning horizon.
